Cache Modes

1. What are Cache Modes?
  • Cache mode determines how data is distributed across the cluster;
  • Ignite supports three cache modes: PARTITIONED, REPLICATED, and LOCAL;
  • Configured via CacheConfiguration.setCacheMode();
2. PARTITIONED Mode (Default)
  • Data is split into partitions and distributed across server nodes;
  • Each key lives on exactly one primary node (plus optional backup nodes);
  • Writes are fast — only the primary and backup nodes are updated;
  • Reads may require a network hop — if the key is on another node, a request is sent over the network;
  • Most scalable mode — adding nodes increases capacity linearly;
  • Best for: large datasets with frequent writes; 
    CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("users");
cfg.setCacheMode(CacheMode.PARTITIONED);
cfg.setBackups(1);
3. REPLICATED Mode
  • Every node holds a full copy of all data in the cache;
  • Reads are always local — no network hop needed;
  • Writes are expensive — every node must be updated;
  • Total storage capacity is limited by the smallest node;
  • Best for: small, read-heavy lookup tables (country codes, configuration data, reference data); 
    CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("countries");
cfg.setCacheMode(CacheMode.REPLICATED);
4. LOCAL Mode
  • Data is stored only on the node that created it — no distribution, no replication;
  • Essentially a local concurrent map backed by Ignite's memory management;
  • Useful for node-local scratch space or temporary computations; 
    CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("localScratch");
cfg.setCacheMode(CacheMode.LOCAL);
5. Choosing a Cache Mode
Criteria PARTITIONED REPLICATED LOCAL
Data size Large (scales with nodes) Small (limited by one node) Small (single node)
Read performance May require network hop Always local Always local
Write performance Fast Slow (all nodes) Fast
Fault tolerance Configurable backups Full replication None
SQL joins Distributed (or colocated) Local Local only
